Jamadar Shahabuddin, Hcgp) This Criminal Revision Petition Is Filed Under Rudrappa S/O Malleshappa Muchchandi vs The State Of Karnataka on 31 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105263382/ 1 Section 397 Of Cr.P.C., Praying To [LEAKAGE_MASK] The Judgment
texts.facts: The case of prosecution is that the Kirana shop of the petitioner was said to be raided by the authorities, where they came to know that the petitioner had stored adulterated salt. Accordingly, the charge sheet was filed before the JMFC, Bagewadi for the offences punishable under Sections 7(1), 16(1)(A) and (B) of the PFA Act. The petitioner appeared before the Magistrate and pleaded guilty. The petitioner was found only with adulterated salt, which is not more cost. Therefore, prayed for allowing the in the petition . But, the first applied Court has awarded only 3 months imprisonment, which is sufficient and therefore, prayed for dismissing the petition. Hence, the State filed an appeal.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the first appellate Court has committed error in enhancing the sentence, even though the petitioner pleaded guilty. It is further provided that the Court, may by adequate and special reasons, impose lesser punishment but shall not less than 3 NC: 2024:KHC-K:6506 months and it may extend to 2 years and fine and the fine shall not be less than Rs.500/-. 8. The first appellate Court has also relied upon the judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of STATE THROUGH INTELLIGENCE OFFICER NARCOTIC CONTROL BUREAU Vs. MUSTAK AHMED ETC. reported in 2015(4) Crimes 143 (SC), where the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that when the law mandates the minimum sentence, the Court has no power to reduce the same by granting any lesser sentence.
